title: Session-settled host close: a new prompt or any Stop closes what the session left open; stale-id observations route to the newest task; notification turns alias, never row
context: 1.38.0 introduced the host close at Stop with a provisional reopen on any later observation. On the live ledger (2026-09-16) three triggers left tasks open forever and their evidence out of the episode record: a prompt interrupted before its Stop (#263), an agent reusing an older task id as the grounding instructs, which reopened a host-closed task no Stop would close again (#266), and background-command notification turns opening empty <task-notification> rows (#269).
decision: Stop still closes the prompt's own task as a host close and persists its record. In addition: (1) settleSessionTasks host-closes every task of the session still open when a new prompt starts (keeping the new task, or the task a notification continues) and when any Stop fires, except tasks with a check-start still inside its timeout plus grace; the caller persists their records. (2) continuationLinks treats an OPEN previous task as the session's current work whatever its age, so the next prompt continues it. (3) appendEvent on a host-closed task routes deliveries/saves/claims/conformance/refusals to the session's newest task when one exists and is open or host-closed; check-start/check stay on the named task (a result must match its start) and reopen it; a task the agent closed is never a routing target. Reopen remains the fallback when no newer task exists. (4) A prompt whose first line is <task-notification> aliases its prompt identity to the session's latest task (report_task_aliases) unless the agent closed that task; identity() resolves aliases, so Stop and hook observations of that turn report to the continued task and no row is opened. Stop still never selects a task by recency for an unknown prompt; the alias is explicit.
consequences: An interrupted prompt's checks and lessons reach the episode record at the next prompt or Stop; hunch task list no longer shows open rows inside a completed chain.
Verification on an old id still reopens that task; the next prompt or Stop settles it.
A new served.db table report_task_aliases (additive, CREATE IF NOT EXISTS).
A late observation from a genuinely continued turn (another hook's block) still reopens the same task when it is the session's newest, as before.
alternatives_rejected: Keep the unconditional reopen and rely on the agent calling finish: the ledger showed agents do not, and an interrupted prompt has no Stop at all.

Have stopHookReport fall back to the session's latest task when the prompt has no task: violates the existing guarantee that Stop never borrows a recent task for an unknown prompt (test 'old hosts never borrow a recent task'); replaced by the explicit alias.
Open a ledger row for notification turns and mark it: still an empty row per background command and an instruction to start a task titled <task-notification>.
Throw on observations naming a host-closed task: would fail the agent's hunch_context mid-turn and lose the observation.

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Leave interrupted tasks open until explicit user action closes them (perpetuates orphaned state)
Route observations to the task that created them (breaks assumption of single current work)
Create separate rows for background notifications (orphans empty records)
Include all commits in git anchoring (obscures user work with metadata noise)
